comments.content: <document version="2.0"><paragraph>I initially glossed over this when it was covered in lecture but while doing the hw I realized that when you're showing the derivation of implicit regularization, we're going in the basis of V.T not V, so while ridge regression technically does suppress principal components of our design matrix with lower singular vectors, implicit reg in gradient descent is acting on the coordinates of the rows of V not our principal components directly. Confused on what the relation is between both spaces now and how early stopping is similar to ridge</paragraph></document>

V-1w actually puts changes the column vector w into the V basis. 

Since V-1 = VT , VTw actually changes the column vector w into the V basis.

comments.content: <document version="1.0"><paragraph>V is not symmetric so the V.T basis is not the same as the V basis. if you write out the matrix vector multiplication, you’re getting a summation of (v.T)_i * w_i where each (v.T)_i is the column vector which is not necessarily the same as v_i.</paragraph></document>

comments.content: <document version="2.0"><paragraph>ohhhhhh I was thinking about the matrix vector multiplication as the linear sum of the columns of V.T but forgot that to project onto basis you need to take dot product which was the point she was trying to make. thanks for that recap!</paragraph></document>
